summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V15.1.2 as modified, moved from 4.0.3 V14.2.5, merged from V14.2.4, and covering V12.3.6. Those three predecessors already asked for a Software Bill of Materials of third-party libraries, that third-party components come from pre-defined trusted and continually maintained repositories, and that the application not include or execute functionality from untrusted sources (unverified CDNs, JavaScript libraries, npm, or server-side DLLs).

Andrew van der Stock filed #512 on 21 February 2019 to reword V12.3.6; that untrusted-source language is the piece the mapping says this inventory control still covers. Git agrees with the mapping on these predecessor IDs, unlike many neighboring V15 slots.

On 21 February 2019 the V12.3.6 reword that closed #512 landed (commit ec703d7b). Three days later Josh Grossman padded V14.2.4 and marked V14.2.5 against Proactive Control C2. On 13 October 2021 136826+cmlh touched V14.2.5 to fix #1066, and jim followed with a V14 Config update on 15 October 2021. 5.0 then combined SBOM inventory with the trusted-repository and untrusted-source clauses into one catalog requirement, adding the "pre-defined, trusted, and continually maintained" phrasing to the SBOM line.

Bankde's #726 (moving reflective file download) is attached via a V12.3.6 move stamp and is not a wording change to this inventory control. Cookie-prefix and SSRF events on other IDs in the timeline are slot reuse.
